title_en: Wang Baofu v. Sanxin Law Firm — dispute over compensation for property damage

full_text_en:
Wang Baofu v. Sanxin Law Firm — dispute over property damage compensation

【Ruling Summary】

According to the provisions of Article 49, Paragraph 1 of the Lawyers Law of the PRC, if a will witnessed by a lawyer is confirmed invalid due to non-compliance with the statutory formal requirements, thereby causing economic losses to the beneficiary of the will, the law firm where the lawyer practices shall bear liability for compensation based on fault.

Plaintiff: Wang Baofu, male, 56 years old, residing at Madian West Village, Haidian District, Beijing.

Defendant: Beijing Sanxin Law Firm, domiciled at South of Nongzhan Hall, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Responsible Person: Liu Cheng, Director of the firm.

The plaintiff, Wang Baofu, filed a lawsuit with the Chaoyang District People's Court of Beijing against the defendant, Beijing Sanxin Law Firm (hereinafter referred to as Sanxin Law Firm), concerning a dispute over property damage compensation.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The will made by the plaintiff's father, Wang Shouzhi, during his lifetime and witnessed by the defendant was confirmed invalid by the court in a succession lawsuit due to the lack of the statutory formal requirement of having two or more witnesses. The plaintiff, as the losing party in the succession lawsuit, not only could not inherit the father's estate according to the will, but also had to pay compensation for the value of the inherited house to other heirs under statutory succession. The defendant was at fault in the process of witnessing the plaintiff's father's will, infringing upon the plaintiff's right to inherit by will, and caused property losses to the plaintiff, for which it should compensate. The plaintiff requests a judgment ordering the defendant to compensate for losses including the compensation for the house value, the agency fee for will witnessing, the agency fees and litigation costs for the two-instance succession lawsuits, totaling RMB 134,893.75.

Defendant's Defense: The matter entrusted to the defendant by Wang Shouzhi was to witness the signature, not to witness the drafting of a will by another person. The defendant, based on Wang Shouzhi's entrustment, only assigned one lawyer to witness Wang Shouzhi's signature. It has fulfilled its obligations and had no fault in the witnessing process. As for the will whose signature was witnessed by the defendant, the defendant had no obligation to advise on whether its content and form complied with legal requirements. The will made by Wang Shouzhi was confirmed invalid because the person who drafted it did not sign it. The defendant was not the drafter of the will and should not bear the legal responsibility of the drafter. In summary, the defendant disagrees with the plaintiff's claims.

The Chaoyang District People's Court of Beijing found the following facts upon trial:

In 2001, Wang Shouzhi, the father of the plaintiff Wang Baofu, signed a "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement" with the defendant Sanxin Law Firm. The agreement stipulated that: Sanxin Law Firm accepted Wang Shouzhi's entrustment and assigned lawyer Zhang He as Wang Shouzhi's agent; the agency matter and scope were: acting as witness; the attorney fee was RMB 6,000; the payment method was cash; the payment time was August 28, 2001; the agreement also included other rights and obligations agreed upon by both parties. Wang Shouzhi signed the agreement, and Sanxin Law Firm affixed its official seal to the agreement, but the agreement was not dated. On September 10 of the same year, Wang Shouzhi also signed a "Power of Attorney for Non-Litigation" with lawyer Zhang He, assigned by Sanxin Law Firm. The content stated: Due to the witnessing matter requiring assistance from a lawyer, Sanxin Law Firm's lawyer Zhang He is specially entrusted as the agent, with the scope of authority being: acting as witness. On September 17, Sanxin Law Firm issued a "Certificate of Attestation", attaching one copy each of Wang Shouzhi's will and Sanxin Law Firm's attestation. The first item of Wang Shouzhi's will was: "I give the part of the unit apartment located at Room 1141, Gate 11, Dormitory of the Clock and Glasses Company, Beitaipingzhuang, Haidian District, Beijing, that belongs to me personally and my inheritance from my wife's estate to my eldest son, Wang Baofu, for inheritance." The content of the attestation was: "Wang Shouzhi, an elderly resident at No. 2, Gate 4, Building 3, Dormitory of the Clock and Glasses Company, Beitaipingzhuang, Haidian District, Beijing, personally signed the foregoing will in our presence. This signature represents his true intention. According to the provisions of Article 55 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, his signing act is true and valid." The signature of the witnessing lawyer Zhang He and the seal of Sanxin Law Firm were affixed at the end. Wang Shouzhi received the "Certificate of Attestation" on September 19.

On December 9, 2002, Wang Shouzhi passed away. In January 2003, the plaintiff Wang Baofu filed a lawsuit with the Haidian District People's Court of Beijing, requesting inheritance of the estate according to Wang Shouzhi's will. On June 30, 2003, the final judgment of the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court determined that: Although the will made by Wang Shouzhi had the signatures of himself and lawyer Zhang He and was affixed with the official seal of Beijing Sanxin Law Firm, the form of the will did not comply with the mandatory requirements for a holographic will or a will made by another person as stipulated by the succession law. It confirmed that Wang Shouzhi's will did not meet the statutory formal requirements for testamentary succession, and ruled that Wang Shouzhi's estate should be handled according to statutory succession. Consequently, Wang Baofu filed this lawsuit, requesting Sanxin Law Firm to compensate for economic losses. After verification and confirmation, under statutory succession, the plaintiff Wang Baofu's inheritance was RMB 114,318.45 less than what he would have received under testamentary succession.

The above facts are confirmed by the following evidence: statements of both parties, the "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement", the "Power of Attorney for Non-Litigation", the "Certificate of Attestation", the reception record of Sanxin Law Firm, the civil judgment (2003) Hai Min Chu Zi No. 3229, and the civil judgment (2003) Yi Zhong Min Zhong Zi No. 5122.

The Chaoyang District People's Court of Beijing held:

A law firm is an institution that relies on engaging lawyers to provide services to clients and obtains corresponding consideration. Succession law provides that a will made by another person shall have two or more witnesses present at the scene, with one of them drafting it, noting the year, month, and day, and signed by the drafter, other witnesses, and the testator. Both lawyers and ordinary citizens have the right to act as witnesses for a will made by another person. However, compared with ordinary citizens, as witnesses, lawyers can use their legal knowledge to serve the testator, ensuring that the will meets legal requirements, which is precisely the desire of the testator who pays consideration to entrust a lawyer as a witness. The plaintiff Wang Baofu's father, Wang Shouzhi, signed an agency agreement with the defendant Sanxin Law Firm, with the purpose of making his will legally effective through the legal services provided by the lawyer. Sanxin Law Firm was aware of this entrustment purpose of Wang Shouzhi and should have assigned two or more lawyers to act as witnesses when Wang Shouzhi made the will, or informed Wang Shouzhi that he still needed other persons to act as witnesses for the will he made to take effect. However, in the "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement" signed by both parties, Sanxin Law Firm only stated that the entrusted matter and scope were "acting as witness". Sanxin Law Firm could not provide evidence to prove that it had informed Wang Shouzhi at the time of signing the agreement that the meaning of "acting as witness" was only to be responsible for Wang Shouzhi's signing act. Therefore, it should be determined that the meaning of "acting as witness" in this case was to witness the will made by Wang Shouzhi. Sanxin Law Firm's defense that it only witnessed Wang Shouzhi's signature could not be adopted due to insufficient evidence. The signing parties of the "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement" were Wang Shouzhi and Sanxin Law Firm. Only Sanxin Law Firm had the right to decide how to perform the agreement signed with Wang Shouzhi. Zhang He was only a lawyer assigned by Sanxin Law Firm and could only act according to the instructions of the firm, without the right to decide how the firm should act. Sanxin Law Firm's argument that the decision to assign only Zhang He to act as a witness was made based on Wang Shouzhi's entrustment to Zhang He could not be sustained.

Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC stipulates: "Citizens and legal persons who, through their fault, infringe upon state or collective property, or infringe upon the property or person of others, shall bear civil liability." When the defendant, Sanxin Law Firm, performed the "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement" signed with Wang Shouzhi, it failed to fulfill its duties as an agent, causing losses to the client and the beneficiary of the will, for which it should bear compensation liability. However, the scope of compensation is limited to the reduced inheritance share of the plaintiff Wang Baofu due to the invalidity of the will. Although Sanxin Law Firm was at fault in performing the agreement, considering that Wang Baofu chose to file a tort action rather than a contract action in this case, and moreover, Wang Shouzhi's heirs are not limited to Wang Baofu alone, the court does not support Wang Baofu's claim for Sanxin Law Firm to refund the agency fee paid by Wang Shouzhi to it. The fault of Sanxin Law Firm in witnessing the will made by Wang Shouzhi did not necessarily cause Wang Baofu to initiate and persist in two-instance succession lawsuits. Therefore, the court also does not support Wang Baofu's claim for Sanxin Law Firm to compensate for the agency fees and litigation costs he incurred in the two-instance succession lawsuits.

Accordingly, the Chaoyang District People's Court of Beijing rendered the following judgment in May 2004:

1. The defendant, Sanxin Law Firm, shall, within seven days after the judgment takes effect, compensate the plaintiff, Wang Baofu, for economic losses totaling RMB 114,318.45.

2. The other claims of the plaintiff, Wang Baofu, are dismissed.

The court acceptance fee for this case is RMB 4,208, of which RMB 412 shall be borne by the plaintiff, Wang Baofu, and RMB 3,796 shall be borne by the defendant, Sanxin Law Firm.

After the judgment, Sanxin Law Firm, dissatisfied, appealed to the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, arguing: According to the agreement signed between Wang Shouzhi and our firm, our firm only provided witnessing for Wang Shouzhi's signature on the will, not for the act of making the will itself. The will was already written by another person for Wang Shouzhi in advance. In the process of performing this "Non-Litigation Entrustment Agency Agreement", Wang Shouzhi suffered no property loss and did not have the right to claim damages for breach of contract. The will made by Wang Shouzhi was confirmed invalid by the court because it did not meet the statutory formal requirements, which had nothing to do with our firm's act of witnessing his signature. Article 58, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC stipulates that an invalid civil act has no legal binding force from the time it was performed. That is to say, from the time the will was made, the appellee, Wang Baofu, never obtained the right to inherit property according to Wang Shouzhi's will. Now the court has determined that Wang Baofu inherits Wang Shouzhi's estate according to statutory succession, which is the right he should enjoy. Wang Baofu has not suffered any tortious loss at all, and therefore does not have the right to claim compensation for tort. The original trial had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law. The appellant requests the second instance to set aside the first item of the original judgment and instead dismiss all of Wang Baofu's claims.

The appellee, Wang Baofu, agreed with the original judgment.

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, upon trial, confirmed the facts found in the first instance.

The issues in dispute in this case are: (1) Did Sanxin Law Firm's "acting as witness" refer to witnessing Wang Shouzhi's act of signing the will, or to witnessing Wang Shouzhi's act of making the will? (2) Did Sanxin Law Firm's witnessing act infringe upon Wang Baofu's civil rights, and should it bear compensation liability?

The Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court held:

Article 2 of the Lawyers Law of the PRC stipulates: "For the purposes of this Law, 'lawyer' refers to a practitioner who has lawfully obtained a lawyer's practice certificate and provides legal services to the society." Article 15, Paragraph 1 stipulates: "A law firm is the practice organization of lawyers." Article 27 stipulates: "When acting as agents in litigation or non-litigation legal matters, lawyers shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of the client within the scope of the entrusted authority." When citizens lack professional legal knowledge and wish to make their actions comply with legal requirements, they often seek help from lawyers. Lawyers are professionals familiar with legal matters who provide legal services to society. When lawyers act as agents in non-litigation legal matters, they shall safeguard the lawful rights and interests of the client within the scope of the entrusted authority. The appellee Wang Baofu's father, Wang Shouzhi, entrusted the appellant Sanxin Law Firm to handle witnessing matters, with the purpose of making his will legally effective through the legal services provided by professionals familiar with legal matters. As an institution specializing in providing legal services, Sanxin Law Firm should have been aware of this purpose of Wang Shouzhi in signing the contract and had the obligation to provide Wang Shouzhi with complete legal services to safeguard the lawful rights and interests of the client. Sanxin Law Firm could not provide evidence to prove that the "acting as witness" agreed upon with Wang Shouzhi was only to witness the identity of the signatory and the authenticity of the signing act; nor could it provide evidence to prove that at the time of signing the contract, it had clearly informed Wang Shouzhi that its attestation was only for the signature and not for the will itself. Therefore, it should bear the adverse consequences of failing to provide evidence. Sanxin Law Firm's appeal argument that it only provided witnessing for the authenticity of Wang Shouzhi's signing act lacks evidentiary support and is not accepted.

Article 49, Paragraph 1 of the Lawyers Law of the PRC stipulates: "If a lawyer causes losses to a party due to illegal practice or fault, the law firm where the lawyer practices shall bear liability for compensation. After compensating, the law firm may recover from the lawyer who acted intentionally or with gross negligence." The essence of Wang Shouzhi's act of making the will was to transfer the property referred to in the will to the appellee, Wang Baofu, for inheritance. Because after accepting Wang Shouzhi's entrustment, the appellant Sanxin Law Firm, in the process of "acting as witness" for Wang Shouzhi's making of the will, failed to provide Wang Shouzhi with complete legal services, resulting in the will made by Wang Shouzhi being confirmed invalid by an effective judgment of the people's court, and Wang Shouzhi's wishes could not be fulfilled. An invalid civil act naturally has no legal binding force from the time it was performed. However, this only means that Wang Baofu cannot lawfully obtain the right to inherit by will. It does not mean that Wang Shouzhi never intended or was unable to transfer his property to Wang Baofu through making a will, let alone that Wang Baofu could not obtain Wang Shouzhi's estate through testamentary succession at all. The fundamental reason why Wang Baofu cannot now inherit Wang Shouzhi's estate according to the will is that Sanxin Law Firm failed to provide Wang Shouzhi with complete legal services, resulting in Wang Shouzhi making an invalid will. The fault of Sanxin Law Firm in performing its duties infringed upon Wang Baofu's right to inherit Wang Shouzhi's estate by will, thereby causing losses to Wang Baofu, for which it should bear compensation liability.

In summary, the findings of fact in the original trial were clear. The judgment, which ordered the appellant Sanxin Law Firm to compensate the appellee Wang Baofu for property losses suffered due to his inability to inherit according to the will, based on Article 106, Paragraph 2 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC, correctly applied the law and was appropriate in its handling, and should be affirmed. The appeal grounds of Sanxin Law Firm are all untenable and should be dismissed. Accordingly, the Beijing Second Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, rendered the following judgment on December 1, 2004:

Dismiss the appeal and affirm the original judgment.

The court acceptance fee for the first instance shall be executed according to the first instance judgment; the court acceptance fee for the second instance is RMB 4,208, to be borne by the appellant, Sanxin Law Firm.

This judgment is final.
